# the contributor audit: simultaneous facet contact and selected-menu certificate

Source: `candidate 810352ec6ea27062`, Sections 1--6. Independent root audit: PASS for the exact equivalence, hinge construction, rigidity implication, and finite sufficient certificate. No unrestricted Gamma lower bound follows yet.

The sampled Jensen inequality for each lower barycentric offset follows by taking the minimum of its affine coordinate on the actual Minkowski combination of the endpoint fibers contained in the anchor fiber. It has the stated direction. The fixed-normal bundle is the convex hull of finitely many actual simplex facets, hence a finite polytope generated by their actual lifted vertices.

If a lifted vertex of type j is not a vertex of one incident bundle polytope, its nontrivial convex representation obeys the lower-coordinate inequalities for EVERY active coordinate l!=j. At the anchor, each coordinate is at its lower bound, so both the pointwise fiber inequalities and the sampled Jensen inequalities are equalities. Each positive summand must therefore be the same type-j vertex at its base. Removing any copy of the anchor leaves a nontrivial anchored relation by other bases with simultaneous equality in all d active offsets. Conversely that relation is a representation in EVERY incident bundle. No relation using incompatible independent facet weights is substituted: the same weights and bases work throughout.

The continuous extensions b_i(z)=min_{x in C_z}lambda_i(x) are convex on the projection. Equality in a positive convex combination implies affinity on the hull of its bases. The source's small-epsilon argument proves this directly and does not assume differentiability or supporting gradients at projection boundaries.

A vertex of the finite bundle polytope is uniquely exposed by an affine functional. The finite gap to the other generating vertices both localizes the hinge near this vertex and excludes all other integer bases. Multiplication by a continuous nonnegative function of the unit normal kills the other finitely many facet normals without changing physical convexity for fixed normal. The support has positive facet measure, including H_0 counting for d=1. Strict captured weights persist on its neighborhood; closed-boundary rows are safely retained only as nonnegative extras. Thus E(W)<=c forces the asserted common contact relation at every vertex whose strict weight exceeds c.

For an actual finite critical menu, optimizing the strict-capture weight over the response polytope and then choosing the corresponding hinge proves the displayed lower certificate. The finite LP dual and extreme-support bound use the already audited b_j=S_j u_j normalization. Empty exposed-vertex lists or low LP values supply no conclusion. The baseline R4, its quadratic perturbation, and the symmetry-selected orbit give different values consistently; none is promoted to a general classification.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
